fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Access Drive; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Multiple Structures; Limited Side Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entry point with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate it quickly in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Clear a turnaround area within the driveway or parking area so emergency vehicles can reverse out without backing onto the road.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain at least 14 feet of vertical clearance and enough width for an emergency vehicle to pass through.
• Cut back shrubs and low branches growing close to both the main residence and the detached structure to reduce the path fire can travel from plants to buildings.
• Thin dense vegetation between the two structures so fire cannot spread directly from one building to the other through continuous plant growth.
• Keep a clear walking path along at least one side of the main residence so responders can reach the rear of the building on foot.
• Post a property map or diagram near the driveway entrance showing the location of both structures, the access drive, and any gates so arriving responders understand the layout immediately.
• Keep any perimeter gates unlocked or secured with a Knox Box or standardized lock so responders are not delayed at the fence line.
• Identify and mark the nearest exterior utility shut-offs on both structures so responders can locate them without searching.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees close to the structure to reduce the path fire can travel upward into the tree canopy.
• Trim or remove scattered shrubs that are directly touching or within a few feet of the structure's walls or foundation.
• Cut back ground vegetation growing up against the base of the structure on all sides.
• Thin scattered trees between the tree cluster and the structure to break up the continuous path vegetation creates toward the building.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and low vegetation on both sides to allow vehicles to pass through without obstruction.
• Remove dead or dry ground vegetation along the edges of the driveway where it runs closest to the structure and tree cluster.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure mowed short and free of accumulated dry plant material.
• Maintain open ground between scattered shrubs so they do not grow together into a continuous mass near the structure.
